chunks: Ibn al-Mutawakkhill narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Yaqtini, from Yunus, from Abdallah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the words of Allah Mighty and Majestic: 'The Fitra of Allah which He created the people upon' — what is that Fitra? He said: It is Islam. Allah created them upon it when He took their Covenant upon Tawhid, saying: 'Am I not your Lord?' and among them were the believer and the disbeliever.

key_terms.أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ: The divine question 'Am I not your Lord?' from the Covenant of Alast
key_terms.فِطْرَة: Innate disposition or natural state created by God

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Fitra in Shia theology according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the 'Fitra' in Surah Ar-Rum as Islam, specifically rooted in the primordial covenant of Tawhid taken from all souls. This narration highlights that the innate disposition toward monotheism is universal, encompassing both believers and disbelievers, thereby grounding Islamic identity in a pre-temporal divine agreement.
